chunks: And indeed it is in the Original Book with Us, Ali is the Wise.

key_terms.أُمِ الْكِتَابِ: The Original or Mother Book, referring to the Preserved Tablet (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz)
key_terms.حَكِيمٌ: The Wise, one of the attributes of Ali
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ: Ali ibn Abi Talib, the first Imam in Shia Islam

ai.seo_question: Who is described as Al-Hakim in the Umm al-Kitab according to Shia exegesis?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, particularly within the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt, this verse is interpreted as referring to Ali ibn Abi Talib, whose name is inscribed in the Umm al-Kitab (Preserved Tablet) alongside the divine attribute 'Al-Hakim'. This highlights his unique spiritual station and wisdom as the inheritor of the Prophet's knowledge, serving as a foundational proof for his Imamate and divine appointment.
